Allergies:
No Known Allergies / Adverse Drug Reactions

Chief Complaint:
Rash, ___ swelling, and SOB.

History of Present Illness:
___ with h/o HCV, vasculitis, HTN, and depression presenting 
with rash and dyspnea. The patient reports that he went to see 
the doctor for his rash today. He feels his breathing has been 
labored for the past 1.5 days and he has been experiencing a 
cough productive of brownish sputum. He feels his breathing gets 
like this often when his 'legs flair up'. He denies F/C, no CP, 
+40 lb weight gain in last 3 weeks. No orthopnea, no PND.  
He was recently hospitalized for a cryoglobulinemia flare ___ 
his HBV. He was treated with steroids and felt well, despite 
increased edema and swelling "everywhere". He had continued his 
prednisone taper and was at 20 mg daily on the day of admission. 
On ___, he reports that one of the workers at the rehab noted 
a rash on his right knee. He feels this rash is c/w his prior 
"cryoglobulinemia flare" and he called to schedule an 
appointment at his PCPs office. There, the patients lung exam 
was significant for expiratory wheezes throughout and given his 
overall presentation, the patient was referred to the ED.  
Initial VS in the ED: 98.0 73 128/54 20 97% RA. Exam notable for 
reports of wheezing. Labs notable for Hct 35.9, Cr 1.3, ALT 51, 
and BNP of 718. Patient was given nebulizer therapy, IV 
steroids, and azithromycin prior to his admission for a COPD 
flair. VS prior to transfer: 97.8 72 132/80 12 94%.  
 
On the floor, the patient is resting comfortably, but is 
diaphoretic. He feels his breathing is much better and his leg 
pain is at its baseline.  
Review of systems:  
(+) Per HPI  
(-) Denies fever, chills, night sweats. Denies headache, sinus 
tenderness, rhinorrhea or congestion. Denied chest pain or 
tightness, palpitations. Denied nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, 
constipation or abdominal pain. No recent change in bowel or 
bladder habits. No dysuria. Denied arthralgias or myalgias.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with h/o HCV, cryoglobulinemia, HTN, and depression p/w new 
nonblanching purpuric rash and wheezing on exam.  

# Purpuric rash: The pt had a recent admission for 
cryoglobulinemia with rash and now represented from ___ 
___ with new medial R knee coalescing petechial patch 
and similar petechiate over buttocks and lover back. Derm was 
consulted and felt the new rash was concerning for LCV vs 
evolving cryoglobulinemia and the purple/dusky areas on lower 
extremities are concerning for the development of retiform 
purpura. A skin biopsy was done of the R medial knee. 
Rheumatology was also consulted and recommended increasing 
prednisone to 60mg daily (the dose he was on 2wks ago at dispo). 
Pt will be seen in ___ clinic to ___ skin biopsy 
and prednisone dosing. 
.
# Wheezing: The pt has no known history of COPD, though does 
have 20pk year history. He says he has had PFTs in the past that 
were "bad." Chronic cough and sputum production unchanged from 
baseline. He does not use inhalers or nebs. It appears that he 
also had wheezing at his last admission and his exam is the same 
as during his last admission with no symptoms. He has no DOE or 
SOB. No fever or chills. He is satting well and does not appear 
to have labored breathing. His presentation overall is 
consistent with COPD flare. Pt was started on azithromycin in ED 
which has been dced. He was on prn ipratroprium/albuterol 
inpatient. Plan to dc on albuterol prn. Should be followed up as 
an outpatient for repeat PFTs to formally diagnose COPD. 

# HCV/Cryoglobulinemia: Patient reports that he has not 
previously followed with a hepatologist and does not know what 
the state of his disease is. He denies current EtOH or IVDU. 
LFTs significant for slightly elevated ALT (51), AST wnl. Recent 
HCV VL 300,443 IU/mL (___) and he is scheduled to follow in 
the liver clinic (with Dr. ___ in ___. 

# Peripheral edema: Pt reports losing 7 lbs since last 
admission, although prior to that he was 40lbs up. Still 
continues to have edema. Likely due to steroid therapy and/or 
chronic stasis. Unlikely CHF given no signs of JVD or crackles 
on exam. He received 20mg IV lasix to help improve the 
pain/swelling. Holding further diuresis given risk for renal 
failure in setting of active cryoglobulinemia  

# HTN: Normotensive during admission. Continued home metoprolol. 
 

# Depression: Mood/affect appear wnl at this time. Continued 
home citalopram, mirtazapine, trazodone. 

# CKD: Baseline Cr ~1.2, Cr 1.1 on discharge. 

# Iron deficiency anema: Hct at baseline, etiology unclear, 
needs further evaluation. Continue iron supplements.

# GERD: Continued home omeprazole.

# Tobacco use: Patient reports not smoking in the last month and 
has been using the nicotine patch. Continued nicotine patch. 

# Alcohol abuse: Pt abstinent ___ with episode of drinking for 
45minutes a few weeks ago due to chronic pain. Pt counseled to 
abstain from alcohol due to increased risk of liver cancer given 
Hep C. Pt will to do AA, planned to go to ___ (sober 
house) after dc from ___. 

# Code: **** FULL CODE ***** (previous notes say DNR/DNI)

# Communication: Patient, wife ___  

# ___ House  

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
- Clean biopsy site with soap, water, then pad dry every day for 
2 weeks. Cover with a thin layer of vaseline and perform 
dressing change every day for 2 weeks.  
- Rheumatology appt in 2 weeks
- Stitches to be removed in 2 weeks at rheum appt. 
- ___ with Hepatology to address treatment of hep c
- If pt remains on prednisone 20mg or greater daily, should be 
started on PCP ppx
- ___ should have outpt ___ of wheezing and concern for COPD 
per PCP

probable cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis
HCV
cryoglobulinemia
COPD exacerbation
